---
title: "C03 Closed-Loop Feedback"
description: "Use measured output and negative feedback to calculate and reduce error."
sidebar: tej
toc: true
execute: {enabled: false}
---

Closed-loop control measures output and compares it with the setpoint. Negative feedback applies a correcting action intended to reduce the error.

$$e=r-y$$

If a thermostat setpoint is $24.0^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and measured temperature is $21.5^\circ\mathrm{C}$, then $e=+2.5^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A heating controller should increase its command.

## Response evidence

Plot setpoint and measured output on the same time axis. Identify only features that the data support:

- rise time
- overshoot
- steady-state error
- cycling or oscillation
- disturbance recovery

Examples include thermostats, cruise control, regulated power supplies, and servo position systems.
